questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I country where I could improve my french language skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was an amazing experience and I would have love to stay even longer if it was possible.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy . However, it was at times a bit of an information overload and I got help from my fellow student to get sure that I didn't overlook anything important.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got a mail with 'guides' from the hosting university on what to do before, under and after the mobility. The administration did also invite to a welcome meeting where we could ask questions and where we received our studentcards.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my on a facebook-group (can't remember the exact group, but can recommend: 'Kots à Bruxelles', 'Colocation Bruxelles'). The room I finally stayed in was the second room I got. The first room a had to share with a person, who turned out to be mentally ill and had a lot of issues, which I didn't want to deal with on my exchange - in an already overwelming situation. I can therefore recommend to really be curious about who you're going to live with (if any) about your mobility - an also to be aware of scammers ofc. I ended up to live in a really nice and cozy flatshare - so it was worth waiting and to be patient.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's great. The transport for students are really cheap (12 euro for a year!), so it's really easy and affordable to go back and forth. And I really liked to live away from uni, so everything in my life didn't circulate around uni-life.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's hard to tell. I was really satisfied, but I only lived with local Belgians who already finished their education - so I didn't really live in a student housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We got a pink form we should fill out in addition to the Learning Agreement. We received a  lot of mails and reminders about that one.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
1) Fill out a temporary learning agreement
2) The first two weeks, the host institution encouraged us to participate to all the courses we found interesting.
3) after two weeks (or so) we had to choose the most interesting courses (and fitting level-wise) and fill out in a final OLA and the 'Pink form' which was a form that signed us up to the written exams at the host institution.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We were assigned a 'course coordinator', who was a professor at the faculty. She could answer questions and was quick to respond.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time the first weeks to explore all the courses as possible (see if it is the right level, if the professor is interesting, to find out what is expected from you as a student in terms of reading, assignments, etc.). In the beginning, I had written one class in my OLA, which sounded interesting in the course catalogue. When I turned up to the class I did not enjoy the way the professor was teaching. Luckily, I then had some other courses I could choose instead.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All classes are only 5 ECTS, so you have to take 6 courses if you need to have 30 ECTS. As a student only used to two or three courses it was a lot of work.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of my classes were not that challenging, with a small curriculum. Others where really challenging, where I had to read a lot and write a long paper in the end. I took most of my classes in french which i can recommend even though you don't have the highest academic level (I'm b2). However, all my teachers allowed my to write my exams in english in the end if you want to do the same thing, it is a good idea to ask your professor if you can write your exam in english).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
In Bruxelles it was mostly the professor speaking in a big auditoire with or without a powerpoint presentation. The students role were mostly to take notes and sometimes to ask question. However, I got the impression that most of the support to the courses comes from former students notes and exam papers.

In Copenhagen we also have our courses in auditoires, but it gets supplementet by classroom teaching, where academic assistents are facilitating the classes. Here we get to ask questions about the lectures and dive into the readings with our fellow students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
GEOG-F414 - Analyse des espaces urbains (Master)
LANGB9071 - 60-HOURS-FRENCH
SOCA-D4996 - Anthropologie de l'environnement (Master)
POLID323 - Introduction to EU Politics
CRIMC201 - Introduction à la criminologie générale
SOCAD473 - Anthropologie de la religion

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Can recommend the 60-HOURS-FRENCH course, where you get to practice you're oral language skills more. Here you also get to meet other exchange students. 

I also really liked the courses: GEOG-F414 - Analyse des espaces urbains (Master)
SOCA-D4996 - Anthropologie de l'environnement (Master), where I experienced the classes as more interactive between the students and the professor.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was not directly unexpected, but Brussels is situated really nicely next to other big cities (Paris, Amsterdam, Rotterdam, etc.), so I went on a lot of trips during the weekends (maybe more than I expected)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport was way less expensive than expected. It is only 12€ for a 12 months transportcard if you're a student younger than 26 years old.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The ULB has a lot of offers: a really cheap sportscard, where you can apply to as many sports as you want each week. The students are really engage aswell in all kinds of clubs ('circles'). I for instant participated in their film club, feminist club, their club for anthropology and sociology students and their small vegestable garden. There is also a lot of comedy shows and concerts at the university cafe 'coin culture'.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Participating in their small vegestable garden is definitely an activity i can recommend. It is a multigenerational project between student and elder people. You get to meet locals while learning a lot about vegestables and managing a compost. They also have a social event for all students once a semester called "disco soup" - it is a must!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Ghent, Bruges, Antwerpen, Paris, Amsterdam, Rotterdam, if you want to experience some of the cities nearby Brussels.
Their is a really nice flea market in Marolles everyday at Place Jeu de Balles and of course a lot of bars with nice local beers;)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Brussels is a really multicultural city - so it went quite quick.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in local clubs and find a place to live with locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes a language barrier was hard, but is was also because I insisted in speaking french.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I find the Belgians really open, curious and interested - that made it easy to participate at activities at the university.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) participate in some of all the student clubs 
2) Try out as many courses as possible in the beginning of the semester
3) Take courses in french if you have an ok level (It is a really nice way to learn french and it is often possible to write your exam in english - so its a win-win)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: In the beginning of the semester, some ULB folklore clubs are 'baptising' the new students, which can be a bit overwhelming to experience, since it's 1,5 month of 'humiliating' activities trying to learn the new students to become independent individuals. (the general opinion on this is very mixed).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It is really hard to tell, since I experience so many rewarding things; Living with only locals, participating i local student clubs and just to meet a lot of exchange students from all over the world. I has broaden my perspective on how it is being a student in many EU countries (and have lucky we are in Denmark to get our studies financed).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first month where I was still new to the city and all a knew was new relationships - Then I missed my friends and my apartment back home a little bit.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
